title: Dispatch LTP 2: Dock Accident Follows the Printed Account
summary: A warning kept workers clear but did not stop the crane from breaking.
author: Clara Vale, Staff Correspondent
paragraphs: The south dock crane failed yesterday at 12:18 p.m. Three crates of glass fell into the water. No one was injured: the dock authority had cleared the landing after receiving the Chronicle’s advance copy. Foreman Edwin Lark confirmed that the future article’s account of the broken chain and the falling cargo was accurate apart from the presence of workers it had expected below.

The council meeting also proceeded broadly as the early edition described. Its unannounced motion concerned repairs to the Northmere Reservoir. Alderman Felix Dorne said he had decided to introduce it before he heard about the paper, though the article quoted one sentence he did not ultimately use.

A second bundle arrived this morning, dated 5 September. Its principal story reports a collision between two streetcars at Bell Lane. The drivers have received copies, and the city has ordered one car held at the depot. Whether the printed accident has now been prevented cannot be known until tomorrow.

Dr. Saye has compared the ink, paper, and type of both bundles with the Chronicle’s stock. They are genuine materials from our pressroom. The words and setting, however, have not passed through our composing room. A fresh scratch across the title type appears in tomorrow’s issue; the matching type in its case remains unmarked.

Mr. Ashcombe has directed the staff to preserve each arriving edition alongside the version actually printed on its date. He says the two records must not be confused. “One tells us what was written before we chose,” he said. “The other tells us what we did.”
